title: Rava son of Rav Idi bar Avin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 136a, Rav Papa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua came to the house of Rava [so it is in the Rosh], son of Rav Idi bar Avin. He prepared for them a third-born calf on its seventh day and they said to him: “Had you waited for it until evening, we would have eaten of it.”
In the Gemara it reads only “the son of Rav Idi bar Avin.”

notes.text: The calf was on its seventh day, rather than the incident being seven days after a son’s birth. Saved Davidson Shabbat 136a calls it third-born and has the guests say to their host that waiting would have let them eat it. The speaker direction and “third-born” wording are corrected accordingly; Rashi’s saved short wording is not claimed to supply that whole explanation.
The bracket naming Rava is Hyman’s report of the Rosh’s reading; the Rosh’s exact text was not independently inspected here.
